name: Jack Newton
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Clio (legal practice management / legal AI software, Vancouver)
profile: Canadian software entrepreneur who co-founded Clio in 2008 with Rian Gauvreau, pioneering cloud-based practice management for lawyers. In Nov 2025 Clio closed the US$1B acquisition of vLex (largest legal-tech M&A ever) alongside a US$500M Series G at a US$5B valuation; Newton is pushing Clio into AI-powered legal research and workflows.
interesting_fact: The vLex deal was described as the largest M&A transaction ever in legal technology, and was announced together with a US$500M Series G at a US$5B valuation.
deep_cut_fact: Before Clio, he was the first software developer at Chenomx, a University of Alberta spinoff building an NMR-based medical diagnostic tool, and took a sabbatical from it to do an MSc in machine learning under Russ Greiner; he started programming around age eight on an IBM 8086.
notes: Very public CEO; author of 'The Client-Centered Law Firm'; frequent conference keynoter (ClioCon). Press route via Clio media team.

name: Jay Scannell
profile: Could not verify any link between a Jay Scannell and MOLOCO. Moloco's published co-founders are Ikkjin Ahn (CEO), David Sehyuk Park and Donghwan Jeon (founded 2013). The only public Jay Scannell found is an exec at Prototype Productions (ex-SkyMall, GiftCards.com), unrelated to Moloco.
notes: Likely a misattribution in the Hurun Unicorn founders list. Verify before any outreach; if the intended person is a Moloco founder, consider Ikkjin Ahn instead (https://www.moloco.com/leadership).

name: Kanav Hasija
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Customer Officer (previously Chief Product Officer), Innovaccer (San Francisco)
profile: IIT Kharagpur graduate who co-founded healthcare data/AI company Innovaccer with Abhinav Shashank and Sandeep Gupta. He built the company's Data Activation Platform underlying its Health Cloud. Innovaccer raised a US$275M Series F in Jan 2025 (backers incl. B Capital, Kaiser Permanente, M12), with press estimates above US$3B valuation.
interesting_fact: Innovaccer's Series F in January 2025 drew strategic health-system investors such as Kaiser Permanente and Banner Health alongside Microsoft's M12 and Danaher Ventures.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he went to the US after IIT Kharagpur to earn a master's in patent law at the University of New Hampshire; as an undergrad he interned at General Electric and was a principal consultant at the student-run Kharagpur Consulting Group.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Abhinav Shashank. Press email is the named press contact on Innovaccer's Jan 2025 release; may change.

name: Jannick Malling
current_role: Co-founder & Co-CEO, Public (Public.com investing platform, New York)
profile: Danish fintech entrepreneur who co-founded the multi-asset investing platform Public with Leif Abraham and runs it as co-CEO. Earlier he worked at Saxo Bank, was Head of Product at CFH Group and co-founded trading-API startup Tradable. Public has recently pushed into direct indexing, bonds and AI-driven 'agentic brokerage' features.
interesting_fact: Public's userbase roughly doubled within days during the January 2021 GameStop frenzy, after having grown 13x the year before, per Malling.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Copenhagen he built websites to organise video-game meetups, and he joined Saxo Bank at 17; he credits that early stint with teaching him speed and user-centric design, and later collaborated with ex-Saxo colleagues on new ventures.
notes: Shares CEO role with Leif Abraham; has spoken publicly (Stanford eCorner) about the co-CEO model. Frequent podcast guest on fintech topics.

name: Anderson Sumarli
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Ajaib Group (Indonesian investment app; also President Commissioner of Ajaib Sekuritas)
profile: Indonesian fintech founder who started Ajaib with Stanford GSB classmate Yada Piyajomkwan; it went through Y Combinator (S18) and became Southeast Asia's first investment-fintech unicorn, offering stocks, mutual funds and crypto. Ajaib also controls Bank Bumi Artha (BNBA). In Aug 2026 it raised a US$270M Series C led by SBI Group at a valuation above its prior ~US$1B mark.
interesting_fact: Ajaib's US$270M Series C (Aug 2026), led by Japan's SBI Group, was reported as Indonesia's biggest tech funding round since 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Ajaib he studied Applied Economics & Management at Cornell (summa cum laude), worked in IBM's Chief Analytics Office (2014-16) and was a BCG consultant (2016-18), then did his MBA at Stanford GSB.
notes: No published press email found on Ajaib's site. Stanford GSB has a case study on Ajaib (useful conversation hook). EY Indonesia 2022 Young Entrepreneur Award; Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2020.

name: Henrik Müller-Hansen
current_role: Founder & CEO, Gelato (on-demand print/production software, Oslo/Fornebu); board member, Patricia Industries (since Jan 2025)
profile: Norwegian-based entrepreneur, former CEO of Tele2 Norway, who launched Optimalprint around 2007 and then Gelato in 2012. Gelato's software and network route print-on-demand orders to local production hubs in 30+ countries, cutting transport distance and waste; it also sells GelatoConnect, a production OS for print factories. Gelato reached a US$1B+ valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Gelato's model is a 'local on-demand production' network: orders are produced in partner factories near the end customer across 30+ countries rather than shipped from a central plant.
deep_cut_fact: Before studying at the Stockholm School of Economics he served as a team leader in a military Underwater Demolition Team; as CEO of Tele2 Norway (2003-06) he roughly doubled revenue from NOK 1.5bn to 3.2bn.
notes: Gelato press releases name a VP PR & Communications (Julie Ryland, 2025) but email addresses are obfuscated on the pages; route via gelato.com news/press section. Tele2 revenue figure is from Gelato's leadership page (https://www.gelato.com/leadership).

name: Artavazd Mehrabyan
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Picsart (creative/AI photo-video editing platform, Armenia/US)
profile: Armenian software engineer who co-founded Picsart with Hovhannes Avoyan and Mikayel Vardanyan (c.2011), serving first as COO and later as CTO. Picsart grew to ~150M monthly active users and 1B+ downloads and became Armenia's first unicorn (2021). He now leads Picsart's push into generative AI, including a commercially safe image model built with Getty Images.
interesting_fact: Picsart reached about 150 million monthly active users and over one billion downloads, and partnered with Getty Images in 2024 on a commercially safe text-to-image model.
deep_cut_fact: Before Picsart he was a chief software architect (incl. at Lycos Europe, Sourcio and Virtual Solutions); he holds two master's degrees: Industrial Engineering from the Armenian National Agrarian University and Computer Science from the American University of Armenia.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Hovhannes Avoyan is the public face. Good angle: Picsart's AI/GPU infrastructure and Armenia's tech ecosystem. Prior-employer list from a job-board company profile; degrees from conference speaker bio.

name: Moses Lo
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Xendit Group (Southeast Asian payments infrastructure, Jakarta)
profile: Australian-born founder (UNSW, UC Berkeley MBA; ex-BCG and Amazon) who co-founded Xendit in 2015; it went through Y Combinator S15 and became the first YC unicorn from Indonesia. Xendit provides payment APIs across Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, and in Nov 2025 launched a Global Account product at the Singapore FinTech Festival.
interesting_fact: Xendit was among the first five Southeast Asian companies accepted into Y Combinator, and became Indonesia's first YC unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: At Radford College in Canberra (Class of 2005) he won debating tournaments and represented Australia at Model United Nations; his advice to students is that 'marks are less important than soft skills.'
notes: Accessible, frequent podcast/conference speaker (Money20/20 Asia). Press email is the named PR & Communications contact on Xendit's Nov 2025 release; based in Jakarta.

name: Wayne Huo
current_role: Co-founder, Amber Group (crypto finance, Hong Kong/Singapore); former CEO of Nasdaq-listed Amber International (AMBR) until Aug 2025
profile: Former Morgan Stanley FX options trader who co-founded Hong Kong crypto trading and wealth platform Amber Group in 2017 with fellow Morgan Stanley alumni; Amber became a unicorn in 2021. He served as CEO of listed affiliate Amber International (Nasdaq: AMBR) until 21 Aug 2025, when Chairman Michael Wu took over the CEO role.
interesting_fact: Amber began as a side project among Morgan Stanley Hong Kong fixed-income traders and reached a US$1B valuation in 2021, with five of its founders having worked together on the same trading floor.
deep_cut_fact: He had been in the workforce only about 18 months, as an FX options trader at Morgan Stanley, when he quit to build Amber; the firm later lured his former boss, Morgan Stanley's Asia FX derivatives head, to join.
notes: Status after Aug 2025 leadership change is unclear: one release says he also resigned as director, while a later 6-K still lists him as a non-independent director (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/amber-international-announces-leadership-changes-to-drive-growth). Crypto angle may be off-topic for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Aidan Corbett
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Wayflyer (revenue-based financing for e-commerce/SMEs, Dublin)
profile: Irish serial entrepreneur (UCC engineering, London Business School MBA) who founded Kubicle and analytics firm Conjura before launching Wayflyer with Jack Pierse in 2019. Wayflyer, which became a unicorn about 20 months after launch, has deployed over €5B to 6,000+ businesses and in 2026 added large credit facilities (e.g. US$250M with ATLAS SP Partners).
interesting_fact: Wayflyer reached unicorn status roughly 20 months after launching; Corbett credits the Netflix culture book 'No Rules Rules', which he says he and Pierse 'swallowed whole'.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a civil servant in Ireland's Department of Communications, Marine and Natural Resources, and his first venture was Kubicle (2013), an online training business teaching professionals Excel and PowerPoint.
notes: Active on podcasts and Web Summit stages. Press contact is Head of Communications Lewis Jones via press@wayflyer.com (2025-26 releases).

name: Anthony Zaccaria
current_role: Co-founder (Chief Commercial Officer per several profiles), Linktree (Melbourne)
profile: Australian entrepreneur who, with brother Alex Zaccaria and Nick Humphreys, ran music/entertainment digital agency Bolster before co-founding link-in-bio platform Linktree in Melbourne in 2016. Linktree grew to tens of millions of users (reported 50M+) and a US$1.3B valuation after its 2022 raise; Anthony has focused on commercial/operations roles and also angel invests.
interesting_fact: Linktree spread with almost no advertising; early users included Selena Gomez, Shawn Mendes, TikTok and Red Bull.
deep_cut_fact: He began in artist management for DJs and bands with his brother; Linktree was born from that work: 'there has to be a better way to direct fans to the content we're producing', since Instagram allowed only one bio link.
notes: Brother Alex Zaccaria (CEO) is the main public face; Anthony keeps a lower profile. Exact current title not confirmed on an official Linktree page.

name: Alfonso De los Rios
current_role: Co-founder of Nowports (Monterrey digital freight forwarder); moved from CEO to President in April 2025 (current title after Oct 2026 CEO change unconfirmed)
profile: Mexican entrepreneur from Monterrey who co-founded Nowports in 2018 with Uruguayan Maximiliano Casal; the YC-backed digital freight forwarder combines logistics with trade finance and software and became a unicorn when he was about 23. He led it as CEO until April 2025 (Fernando Poitevin succeeded him; Casal returned as CEO in Oct 2026).
interesting_fact: Nowports reached a US$1B+ valuation in 2022, making De los Ríos one of Latin America's youngest unicorn founders at around age 23; the company has raised roughly US$250M in equity.
deep_cut_fact: He started coding at 11, and his first 'build' was a modification of Minecraft; he left university in his first semester, which took him to Silicon Valley where he met co-founder Max Casal.
notes: Role change sources: April 2025 (https://www.descubre.vc/noticia/nowports-anuncia-relevo-en-su-direcci-n-general-2025-04-22) and Oct 2026 Casal return (https://clusterindustrial.com.mx/maximiliano-casal-vuelve-como-ceo-de-nowports-para-impulsar-una-nueva-etapa-ai-native/). Nicknamed 'Poncho'. Received Nuevo León's Entrepreneurial Merit Medal. No published press email found.

name: Brynne Rojas
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Habi (proptech / iBuyer, Bogotá; operates in Colombia and Mexico)
profile: Brynne McNulty Rojas, a Miami-born, Harvard MBA, ex-Goldman Sachs real estate investor and ex-McKinsey consultant, co-founded Habi in Bogotá in 2019 with Merqueo co-founder Sebastián Noguera. Habi uses algorithmic pricing to buy, renovate and resell used homes and became Colombia's second unicorn (2022, US$200M round); in March 2026 it acquired Mexican broker-tech startup Pulppo.
interesting_fact: Habi prices tens of thousands of homes a month (30,000+ per month in 2021) and makes most of its offers automatically; its sales team rings a cowbell whenever a transaction is signed.
deep_cut_fact: She and Sebastián Noguera were selected as Endeavor's 100th and 101st entrepreneurs in Colombia (Habi was Endeavor Colombia's 54th company); before Habi she was VP of Global Corporate Strategy at hospitality startup Selina.
notes: Publicly known as Brynne McNulty Rojas. Habi's site lists only a general customer address (contacto@habi.co), no press email found. Habi founded in Bogotá; idea came from her own struggle to find a home remotely when moving to Colombia.

name: Sachin Nayyar
current_role: Founder, CEO & Chairman, Saviynt (identity security, El Segundo, CA)
profile: Serial identity-security entrepreneur who founded Vaau (acquired by Sun Microsystems, where he became Chief Identity Strategist), then Securonix (SIEM; US$1B+ Vista-led growth investment in 2022) and Saviynt. He stepped back to executive chairman at Saviynt in 2018 and returned as CEO in 2023; in Dec 2025 Saviynt raised US$700M led by KKR at about a US$3B valuation.
interesting_fact: Saviynt's US$700M Series B (Dec 2025), led by KKR with Sixth Street Growth, TenEleven and Carrick Capital, valued the identity-security company at roughly US$3B and was pitched as making identity 'the foundation for the AI era'.
deep_cut_fact: He served five years as Board Chair of the Health Information Sharing & Analysis Center (H-ISAC), the healthcare sector's cyber-threat-sharing body; per CEO Magazine he sold his first company, Vaau, to Sun Microsystems at age 28.
notes: Founded both Saviynt and Securonix. PR handled by agency Inkhouse. Vaau-at-28 detail from https://digitalmag.theceomagazine.com/sachin-nayyar/ (page blocked to fetch; seen in search summary).

name: Jonathan Ellis
current_role: Founder & CEO, Brokk (AI coding tools; product now marketed as SlopCop at slopcop.com)
profile: Co-founder and former CTO of DataStax and first chair of the Apache Cassandra project. He and Matt Pfeil left Rackspace in 2010 to found Riptano in Austin (renamed DataStax), the commercial Cassandra company later pivoted to real-time data for AI and acquired by IBM in 2025. He now runs Brokk, building static-analysis and review tooling for AI coding agents.
interesting_fact: He became the first chair of Apache Cassandra when it graduated from the Apache incubator, and directed the project from 2010 until stepping down in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cassandra, around 2005 he built a multi-petabyte storage system for backup service Mozy using Reed-Solomon encoding; a PyCon talk about it led Rackspace to hire him, where evaluating NoSQL databases drew him to Cassandra.
notes: Highly technical; writes the company blog himself (e.g. Nov 2026 post on cost-efficient coding with expensive models). brokk.ai now redirects to slopcop.com; company has a public Discord linked from the site. Strong data-infrastructure angle for the podcast.

name: Russell D'Souza
current_role: Co-founder, SeatGeek (ticketing marketplace and primary-ticketing platform, New York); previously President
profile: Dartmouth '07 history major who, after a short stint in management consulting, co-founded SeatGeek in 2009 with college roommate Jack Groetzinger, initially as a ticket-price comparison engine. SeatGeek moved into resale and, after buying TopTix in 2017, primary ticketing for teams such as the Saints, Pelicans and MLS/NFL clubs. He remains the company's co-founder spokesman, e.g. on its Dec 2025 Google agentic-search integration.
interesting_fact: SeatGeek's founders were not computer science majors: D'Souza studied history and Groetzinger economics, and they began by building a site that compared resale ticket prices.
deep_cut_fact: Before SeatGeek, he and Groetzinger, who were Dartmouth roommates and fraternity brothers in Chi Gamma Epsilon, ran Scribnia, a web app that recommended bloggers to readers.
notes: Goes by Russ D'Souza. Sports Business Journal Forty Under 40 (2019). Current exact title beyond 'co-founder' not confirmed. Roommate/fraternity detail from Dartmouth Alumni Magazine (Sep-Oct 2024).

name: Omair Tariq
current_role: Founder & CEO, Cart.com (unified commerce and logistics/fulfillment platform, Houston)
profile: Pakistan-born, Dubai-raised entrepreneur who moved to Houston as a teen, was an early employee and later COO of Blinds.com (acquired by Home Depot in 2014), then helped grow Home Depot's online business before founding Cart.com in 2020. Cart.com offers e-commerce software, marketplace management and a nationwide fulfillment network; in March 2026 it raised a US$180M growth investment led by Springcoast Partners.
interesting_fact: Cart.com raised US$180M in March 2026 from Springcoast Partners, and in 2025 helped nine-figure brands reshore millions of units within days amid shifting US trade policy.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Pakistan and raised in Dubai, he moved to Houston as a teenager; his entrepreneurial path included starting a jewelry business before he joined Blinds.com as an early employee.

public_contacts.value: Carly Berns, Berns Communications Group: cberns@bcg-pr.com

notes: Houston-based and active in the local innovation scene (Houston Innovators Podcast). Cart.com moved HQ to Austin in 2021 and back to Houston in late 2023. Logistics/warehouse network angle is relevant to energy/infrastructure themes.

name: Don Burnette
current_role: Founder, CEO & Director, Kodiak AI (Kodiak Robotics; autonomous trucking, Mountain View; Nasdaq: KDK)
profile: Autonomous-vehicle engineer (UF electrical engineering, CMU robotics master's) who was a software tech lead on Google's self-driving project (now Waymo), co-founded self-driving truck startup Otto (bought by Uber in 2016), and founded Kodiak in 2018. Kodiak went public via SPAC in 2025 and runs customer-owned driverless trucks hauling frac sand in the Permian Basin for Atlas Energy Solutions.
interesting_fact: Kodiak's trucks run fully driverless for Atlas Energy Solutions in the Permian Basin, hauling frac sand to wellsites around the clock; Atlas plans to grow the driverless fleet to 100 trucks by mid-2027.
deep_cut_fact: Before Kodiak he co-founded Otto, described in Kodiak's investor materials as the first self-driving truck startup, after starting as a software tech lead on Google's self-driving car project; he holds a robotics master's from Carnegie Mellon.
notes: Excellent energy-podcast fit: driverless trucking in oilfield logistics (Permian frac sand). Frequent speaker at CES, FreightWaves and SAE events. First Kodiak/Atlas driverless delivery: Jan 2025 (https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/24/kodiak-has-made-its-first-driverless-truck-deliveries-to-customer-atlas-energy).

name: Mike Cessario
current_role: Founder & CEO, Liquid Death (canned water and beverages, Santa Monica)
profile: Former ad-agency creative director and punk-scene skateboarder who launched Liquid Death in 2019, marketing canned mountain water like an energy drink or beer brand. It hit a US$1.4B valuation in March 2024 on US$263M 2023 retail sales, expanded into iced teas, sparkling and (Jan 2026) energy drinks, and its in-house agency Death Machine now takes outside clients.
interesting_fact: The idea dates to the 2009 Vans Warped Tour, where he saw bands drinking water out of empty Monster Energy cans; the brand's banned 2019 launch video drew 3 million views before the product even shipped.
deep_cut_fact: As a teen in the punk scene outside Philadelphia he booked gigs, made flyers and planned shows, which he says taught him to run a small business; to make Liquid Death he cold-called canneries and ended up with an Austrian canning facility.
notes: Hometown is given variously as 'Delaware native' (Wikipedia) and 'grew up just outside Philadelphia' (Entrepreneur). Beware lookalike domain liquiiddeath.it.com. Very active on podcasts and keynotes; strong brand/marketing angle.

name: Danny Jenkins
current_role: CEO & Co-founder, ThreatLocker (zero-trust endpoint security, Orlando, FL)
profile: Irish-born cybersecurity entrepreneur who started in IT in 1997, co-founded Dublin email-security SaaS MXSweep (sold to j2) and led Sirrustec (sold to Censornet in 2014). In 2017 he co-founded ThreatLocker in Orlando with Sami Jenkins and John Carolan, built around 'default deny' allowlisting; it serves 50,000+ businesses and raised a US$190M Series F in 2026, bringing total funding to nearly US$500M.
interesting_fact: ThreatLocker was born after he witnessed a phishing attack that nearly destroyed a company, leading him to build a 'default deny' model where nothing runs unless explicitly approved.
deep_cut_fact: Long before ThreatLocker he co-founded MXSweep, a Dublin-based email and internet security SaaS provider later sold to j2, and was CEO of white-label email-security firm Sirrustec, sold to Censornet in 2014.
notes: Frequent podcast guest and keynote host at ThreatLocker's Zero Trust World conference. Has said in interviews he left school at 15 for an IT apprenticeship (seen in search summaries of interviews, e.g. https://www.scworld.com/podcast-episode/3596-how-to-start-a-company-when-you-dont-want-to-a-journey-from-founder-to-cto-to-ceo-danny-jenkins-fs-9; not independently verified).
